newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy mulling transfer of SGS-Thomson stake.
newsitem.headline: Italy mulling transfer of SGS-Thomson stake.

text.p: The Italian government is studying whether to transfer the 35 percent stake in SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV held by state holding IRI to IRI's engineering unit Finmeccanica, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said.
Prodi was attending the official opening of an eight-inch wafer plant of the Franco-Italian semiconductor producer.
"We are thinking deeply about it," Prodi said in reply to a question by reporters.
A stake of 35 percent in SGS-Thomson is held by France's Thomson SA while 30 percent of shares are on the market. The group is listed in Paris and New York.
The Italian press has reported that the government was considering the transfer from IRI to allow Finmeccanica to rebalance its debt/equity ratio.
Finmeccanica had 1996 net debt of 5.133 trillion lire, against 4.878 trillion in 1995, with net equity of 4.447 trillion lire.
